page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 capabilities.

Benchmark data indicates that the n1-standard-8 delivers modest performance characteristics. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the weak or poor categories, with a Geekbench single-core score of 923.0 and a multi-core score of 3531.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block read (45.37 GB/sec) and write (34.65 GB/sec) operations, though small-block cached reads are weak at 324.06 GB/sec. Cryptography and compression tasks are similarly constrained, with single-threaded gzip compression rated as poor at 19.07 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 represents an older hardware class with lower resource density and lower performance-per-vCPU compared to newer generations. The lack of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators limits its utility for high-throughput database systems or machine learning training. However, with its balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, it is suitable for general-purpose workloads such as basic web serving, light text processing, and small-scale application hosting where high-performance compute is not a primary requirement.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 30.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. It contains 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, but lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers, with weak single-core and multi-core CPU scores, and poor compression and text processing throughput. However, it maintains average performance in large-block memory bandwidth and ray tracing. Given its moderate resource allocation and legacy hardware profile, the n1-standard-8 is best suited for basic general-purpose workloads, light web serving, and development environments that do not require high-performance compute or local NVMe storage.
